script: My friend called me a betrayer—yet the truth stunned everyone.. I was at Emma's birthday dinner, five of us—me, Emma, Pedro, Faith, and Zoey—ready to celebrate. I am 24, self‑employed, and just leaving a higher‑pay job, so cash was tight. Emma and I had already decided to cancel the dinner because none of us could afford it. Pedro was on his high‑energy, "let's finalize this" vibe all day. When I told him we were breaking up, he asked, "Are you asking me for money?" I said nope, just explaining why we were canceling. Then he dropped the "use my brand‑new credit card, I need that sign‑up bonus." We shook on it: he'd put my meal and half of Emma's on his card, and I'd pay him back Monday. He also said he'd drive me home after. Faith was stuck at work, so we waited to order until she got there. Pedro, meanwhile, ordered three appetizers for himself and ate them while we waited. When Faith finally showed up, we ordered. Pedro even nudged Emma to add a caviar bump. I stepped outside for a cigarette. The restaurant only has one entrance, and I was sitting right outside it. When I came back in, Pedro was gone. Everyone thought he'd just said goodbye to me outside, but he hadn't. I quietly asked the waiter what Pedro had paid for. Only his own appetizers. If he'd left before we ordered, I'd just not order because I couldn't afford it. But he stayed through ordering, knew the deal, so I had no reason to think I suddenly needed to pay. I couldn't reach my boyfriend or parents, so I told Faith what happened. She offered to cover it, but after checking her account she didn't have enough either. Between the two of us, we scraped together every dollar we had to cover the bill. We couldn't even tip the waiter, which still feels like a bruise. Faith had to drive me home because Pedro had left. A few days later, Pedro called me and said I was the asshole for "feeling entitled to his money." I told him I thought he was the asshole because he proposed the arrangement, stayed through ordering, then left without warning and only paid for himself, leaving me scrambling to cover my meal and without my ride home. He laughed and called me entitled. So…am I the jerk?
